newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-SRI LANKA SNIFF TEST WIN IN NZ'S DISARRAY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA SNIFF TEST WIN IN NZ'S DISARRAY.

text.p: The Sri Lankan cricket team head into Friday's first test against New Zealand with every confidence of winning, despite their lack of match practice on tour.
The Kiwis are in disarray after captain Lee Germon was unceremoniously dumped following their one-day series draw and 2-0 nil test series loss against England.
The home side's new skipper is Stephen Fleming, at 23 New Zealand's youngest ever test captain, and the one-day World Cup holders believe the change may unsettle their opponents.

"I think they will take a little time (to get used to it), and I hope we can capitalise on the weaknesses they have," Sri Lanka captain Arjuna Ranatunga told Reuters in a telephone interview on Wednesday.
"We haven't had any good cricket, only two days on tour, so that's not ideal preparation for a test match. But the boys are very keen, they are very confident," he said.

Rain conspired to rob the tourists of a vital warm-up match against New Zealand A this week, and their only game here so far has been a two-day non-first class game against provincial side Northern Districts, which they drew.

But New Zealand's form this summer has hardly got the Sri Lankans quaking in their shoes. The thrashing by England in the recent test series exposed New Zealand's inconsistent batting line-up and ordinary bowling attack.
In contrast, Sri Lanka have batsmen of proven international class such as Aravinda de Silva, Hashan Tillekaratne, and old hand Ranatunga himself.
"I think we have a very good all-round side. We have a very strong batting line-up and most of the top batsmen have been getting a lot of runs back home," Ranatunga said.
"And the bowling has been very good."

In one brief outing on tour so far, Sri Lankan strike bowler Chaminda Vaas has already given the New Zealanders cause for concern. He took six wickets for 22 runs against Northern Districts, including a hat-trick.
The tourists also rate unknown 18-year-old Nuwan Zoysa highly and are eager to get him into the international arena.
Ranatunga plucked the tall, lanky fast bowler from the obscurity of schoolboy cricket eight months ago.

"He has a lot of potential. He has to get into the big league as soon as possible to get used to it because he has a lot of talent," Ranatunga said, hinting that Nuwan was likely to play in the first test.
"It looks like he has a very good chance of playing, but we haven't picked the side so far," he said.
New Zealand have already named their 18-year-old, offspinner Daniel Vettori, after a promising test debut against England.
But New Zealand have had a dismal summer to date.
After their test losses to England, they only just managed to salvage a 2-2 draw in the one-day series by winning the final two matches. The third match was tied.
